idiom_name: plain state struct owned by the frame function (immediate-mode egui/iced); Rc<RefCell> handles for retained toolkits
implementation_notes: Rust's GUI mainstream is immediate mode: the application owns a plain state struct, the frame function reads it to draw and mutates it in response to input, and each frame rebuilds the view from it - egui's documentation states plainly that it does not store widget state for you and that keeping the state between frames is the caller's responsibility. That struct is the presentation model and the command methods are ordinary impl methods, testable without any UI; the classic observer/binding half is largely unnecessary because the redraw is unconditional. Where retained widgets are used (gtk-rs), the model is shared behind Rc<RefCell<T>> and connected through glib signals, which brings the hand-written notification and lifetime work back.
pitfalls: Callbacks handed to a retained toolkit must be 'static, so the state reaches them through Rc<RefCell<_>> - and borrowing it mutably inside a handler that also draws it panics at runtime (already borrowed).
Rc is not Send: the model cannot be shared with worker threads; use Arc<Mutex<_>> or send commands/results over a channel and keep the UI on its own thread.
Immediate mode re-derives everything each frame, so expensive derived values (sorting, formatting) are recomputed many times per second unless memoised deliberately.
